about: Port has been part of Brotherhood’s cellar for more than 150 years. When John Jaques handed the Washingtonville winery to his sons in 1858, it was already making some fifteen styles and storing about 35,000 gallons of wine, port and brandy in hand-dug underground cellars. Renamed Brotherhood in 1886, it survived Prohibition making sacramental wine and, from its first commercial vintage in 1839, has never stopped producing, which is why it calls itself America’s oldest winery. Its traditional specialties, Port among them, were kept when the premium varietal line was added in 1987.

This ruby is made the classic way: red grapes are partly fermented on their skins, then fermentation is stopped by adding fine brandy, which leaves natural grape sugar in the wine and raises the alcohol to about 18 percent. After filtering, it is blended and aged in casks that have long held port and drawn off through a modified solera, a system of continuous blending across many years. The result is sweet, rich and velvety, with dark fruit and chocolate, made for dessert, blue cheese or a cold night.
facts: In aged port casks, blended through a modified solera
